messages.subject: Update/ modifiy multilevel model
parts:
Dear all,

Since the modindces command is not working for my model (https://mail.google.com/mail/u/0/#inbox/FMfcgzGkZQSxfkRhLpGckWnPnTwMwBSM), I have to test all possible residual correlations against one another to see which improves the chisquare value the most. Since there are > 100 combinations, I have to do this using a loop. 

For this, I have tried out two options so far which did not work with the multilevel model.

  1. Update function: If I want to add a residual correlation, I cannot use update(fit, add= item_1 ~~ item_2) because I do not know how to specify on which level the residual correlation should be added. 
  2. Based on an earlier post (https://groups.google.com/g/lavaan/c/thKIUdEjssw), I changed the residual correlations in the parameter table using lavaanify. Yet it seems that for multilevel models it is not possible to a parameter table as model input as I get the following error: Error in Mu.W.tilde[ov.idx[[1]]] <- Mu.W : Replacement has a length of 0

Does anyone know to solve the above-described problems or have a different idea of how to modify the model.syntax of a multilevel model?

Many thanks in advance!

Anabel

messages.subject: Re: Update/ modifiy multilevel model
parts:
In case that this may help to answer my question, here is some example data and code:
library(lavaan)
id <- rep(1:50, each=21)
item_1 <- rnorm(1050, 2.5, 1)
item_2 <- rnorm(1050, 1.7, 0.8)
item_3 <- rnorm(1050, 3.4, 1.2)
item_4 <- rnorm(1050, 2.1, 0.9)
dat <- cbind(id, item_1, item_2, item_3, item_4)

model <- '
level:1 
v =~ item_1 + item_2 + item_3 + item_4

level:2 # I’m only interested in level 1, so level 2 consists of a saturated model 
item_1 ~~ item_1 + item_2 + item_3 + item_4
item_2 ~~ item_2 + item_3 + item_4
item_3 ~~ item_3 + item_4
item_4 ~~ item_4'

fit <- cfa(model, data =dat, cluster ="id")

# First option: using the update-command:

update(fit, add= item_1 ~~ item_2)

# Second option: using the parameter table 

model_res <- '
level:1 
v =~ item_1 + item_2 + item_3 + item_4
item_1 ~~ item_2 # this residual correlation should be changed in the loop 

level:2 
item_1 ~~ item_1 + item_2 + item_3 + item_4
item_2 ~~ item_2 + item_3 + item_4
item_3 ~~ item_3 + item_4
item_4 ~~ item_4'

par_table <- lavaanify(model_res) # residual correlation is stored in row 5
par_table$lhs[5] <- "item_1"
par_table$rhs[5] <- "item_3"
fit <- cfa(par_table, data= dat, cluster= "id")

messages.author: 3fe90052fbf2f899
messages.subject: Re: Update/ modifiy multilevel model
parts:
I have to test all possible residual correlations against one another to see which improves the chi-square value the most.

That is unlikely to lead to a generalizable model.  Consider reading this paper for both a theory-based idea and a useful method:

http://dx.doi.org/10.1080/10705511.2013.769390

1. Update function: If I want to add a residual correlation, I cannot use update(fit, add= item_1 ~~ item_2) because I do not know how to specify on which level the residual correlation should be added.

I would assume the same way you specify the rest: it has to be a character string, and you can flag the level of a particular parameter.

add_this <- ' level:1
item_1 ~~ item_2 '
update(fit, add = add_this)

But that does not appear to work.  Instead, it places equality constraints across levels on the residual variances of those 2 indicators.

model <- '
    level: 1
        fw =~ 1*y1 + 1*y2 + 1*y3
    level: 2
        fb =~ 1*y1 + 1*y2 + 1*y3
'
fit <- sem(model, data = Demo.twolevel, cluster = "cluster")
add_this <- ' level:1
  y1 ~~ y2 '
parTable(update(fit, add = add_this))

Probably a bug, so I reported it on GitHub.

https://github.com/yrosseel/lavaan/issues/216

1. Based on an earlier post (https://groups.google.com/g/lavaan/c/thKIUdEjssw), I changed the residual correlations in the parameter table using lavaanify. Yet it seems that for multilevel models it is not possible to a parameter table as model input as I get the following error: Error in Mu.W.tilde[ov.idx[[1]]] <- Mu.W : Replacement has a length of 0
You would really need to make sure all the necessary columns are in that table.  But this shouldn't be necessary.
Does anyone know to solve the above-described problems or have a different idea of how to modify the model.syntax of a multilevel model?

Instead of using lavaanify(), just specify the syntax in pieces and use c() to concatenate them.  Something like this:

```
L1 <- ' Level: 1
... '
L2 <- ' Level: 2
... '
residCorr  <- expand.grid()  # or outer() or combn(), any trick to get all possible combinations of items
for (loop over the combinations) {
  aug <- paste() # paste the 2 indicators with "~~" in between
  aug_syntax <- c(L1, aug, L2)
  aug_fit <- lavaan(aug_syntax, data =  ...)
}
```
